description: Streamlit advanced framework layer: multipage app shell with sidebar, tabs, caching, Plotly charts, and a typed pydantic-settings module.

buildHints.whenToUse: Data dashboards, internal analytics tools, ML model explorers, or any product where the primary surface is a Python-driven web UI backed by pandas/plotly data.
firstSteps: Run `pip install -r requirements.txt` then `streamlit run app.py` — the app serves on port 8501 with the Overview/Detail/About tab layout immediately visible.
All settings (headline, service name, port) are read from `APP_*` env vars via the `Settings` class in `app.py`; set them in a `.env` file or your deployment environment.
Add new pages by dropping `pages/<number>_<Title>.py` files — Streamlit auto-registers them in the sidebar in numeric order; follow the pattern in `pages/1_analysis.py`.
Heavy data loads should use `@st.cache_data(ttl=...)` for DataFrames and `@st.cache_resource` for database connections — both are demonstrated in `app.py`.
Run `node validate-streamlit.mjs` to verify the scaffold is wired correctly before deploying.
gotchas: `st.set_page_config()` must be the first Streamlit call in every page file, including each file under `pages/`; calling anything else first raises a StreamlitAPIException.
`pydantic-settings` v2 requires `model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix=...)` — the deprecated inner `class Config` style raises warnings and may fail strict linters.
Streamlit re-runs the entire script on every widget interaction; keep heavy computation inside `@st.cache_data` / `@st.cache_resource` to avoid re-fetching on each slider move.
The `.streamlit/config.toml` `port` placeholder (`{{port}}`) must be replaced at compose time — leaving the literal string causes Streamlit to fail to parse the config.
architectureNotes: Each file under `pages/` is an independent script; do not import from `app.py` — share helpers via a separate module (e.g. `lib/data.py`) imported by both.
The `Settings` class is the single source of truth for env-driven config; extend it rather than scattering `os.getenv` calls across page files.
